key_insight: Sequential magnetic alignment and liquid-metal gap bridging create vertical heat pathways in a soft composite while preserving lateral electrical insulation.
engineering_relevance: The composite offers a compliant thermal coupling material for skin-conformal electronics, wearable thermoelectric generators, and heat-spreading pads.
method: Magnetically align Ni microparticles in air before polymer infiltration to form densely packed vertical pathways.
Infiltrate the scaffold with a liquid-metal/Ni mixture to bridge gaps and reduce interparticle thermal resistance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 7.5 W/(m·K) through-plane thermal conductivity, lateral electrical conductivity below 10⁻¹² S/m, and approximately 160 kPa mechanical compliance.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether thermal performance and lateral insulation remain stable under repeated stretching.
paper_title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics
